text.en:
In Mala's village the well water was going down every summer.
Her teacher said, "Water, air, soil, forests and coal are gifts of nature. They are called natural resources."
"Then we must use them carefully," said Mala.

Things that nature gives us and that we use are natural resources. Air, water, soil, sunlight, forests, minerals and coal are examples.
Some resources renew themselves: sunlight, wind, water and forests (if we plant trees) are renewable. They are not used up easily.
Others took millions of years to form and will run out: coal, petroleum, natural gas and minerals are non-renewable. We must use them carefully.
We can protect resources by saving water and electricity, planting trees, reusing and recycling things, and not wasting food or fuel.
Solar energy and wind energy are clean renewable sources. They do not make smoke.
Air, water, soil, forests, coal and sunlight come from nature. They are natural resources.
Sunlight, wind and water can be used again and again. They are renewable.
Coal and petroleum took millions of years to form and will run out. They are non-renewable.
We can save resources by saving water, planting trees and recycling.

problem.en: Is coal renewable or non-renewable? Give a reason.

text.en: Coal formed over millions of years from plants buried long ago.

why.en: It takes extremely long to form.

text.en: We use it much faster than nature makes it.

prompt.en: A friend says water cannot finish because it is everywhere. What will you tell him?

requiredIdeas.en: Clean, usable water is limited, and wells and rivers can dry up.
We should save water and not waste it.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking all natural resources are unlimited.

points.en: Renewable resources are not used up easily; non-renewable ones will run out.
We should save, reuse and recycle.
